governing_statute.value: No comprehensive statute found. Idaho Code 44-1801 to 44-1812 gives firefighters bargaining rights.
governing_statute.quote: The firefighters in any city, county, fire district or other political subdivision in the state of Idaho shall have the right to bargain collectively with their respective cities, counties, fire districts or political subdivisions

scope_of_bargaining.quote: in such collective bargaining process as to wages, rates of pay, working conditions and all other terms and conditions of employment.

impasse_procedure.value: For firefighters: issues unresolved 30 days after the first meeting go to a fact-finding commission, which issues a written recommendation (ss. 44-1805 to 44-1810)
impasse_procedure.quote: In the event that the bargaining agent and the corporate authorities are unable, within thirty (30) days from and including the date of their first meeting, to reach an agreement on a contract, any and all unresolved issues shall be submitted to a fact finding commission.

strike_legality.value: Firefighters may not strike or honor a picket line during the term of a written contract. No general public-employee strike statute was captured.
strike_legality.quote: Upon consummation and during the term of the written contract or agreement, no firefighter shall strike or recognize a picket line of any labor organization while in the performance of his official duties.

agency_fee_status.value: Not collectible from nonconsenting public employees under Janus v. AFSCME (2018).
agency_fee_status.quote: For these reasons, States and public-sector unions may no longer extract agency fees from nonconsenting employees.
agency_fee_status.pinpoint: Janus v. AFSCME, Council 31, 585 U.S. 878 (2018), Part VII
